outcome: No proof, disproof, partial resolution, or bound movement on the four exponentials conjecture was found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains fully open, exactly as it has been since the 1960s.
summary: I searched broadly for any development on the four exponentials conjecture — the statement that given ℚ-linearly-independent pairs {x1,x2} and {y1,y2} of complex numbers, at least one of e^(x1y1), e^(x1y2), e^(x2y1), e^(x2y2) is transcendental — in the window since 26 January 2024. This is a long-standing (Schneider 1957 / Lang-Ramachandra era) open problem in transcendental number theory, a special case of Schanuel's conjecture, and known to be very hard: the six-exponentials theorem's proof technique 'just misses' reducing to four. Searches in both English and French (for 'conjecture des quatre exponentielles', since much of the literature is French, e.g. Waldschmidt, Diaz) turned up only background/survey material: the current Wikipedia and MathWorld articles, Waldschmidt's 2023 survey chapter 'The Four Exponentials Problem and Schanuel's Conjecture' (Springer, in a 2023 volume, so before the window), a 1997 JTNB article by Guy Diaz that is entirely pre-window, and unrelated recent arXiv papers that surfaced only because they share incidental terms ('four exponential terms', Goldbach summatory function, etc.) with the query but do not address this conjecture at all. Waldschmidt's most recent publications (checked via his personal publication list) as of 2025 concern Schanuel's conjecture for elliptic/quasi-elliptic functions, an adjacent but distinct topic, not the four exponentials conjecture itself, and are about a related problem rather than a case or resolution of this one. I also checked for any AI-system involvement (AlphaProof, AlphaEvolve, LLM-driven formal proof search papers) and found no connection whatsoever to this specific conjecture — those systems' publicized work (IMO problems, algorithm discovery, other number-theoretic bounds) does not mention or touch the four exponentials conjecture. I am satisfied this is a genuine 'nothing happened' case: the conjecture is exactly as open now as it was in January 2024, and no AI system has been reported to have engaged with it at all. This agrees with the triage's 'none' verdict.
competing_reading: None found. There is no genuinely ambiguous case or variant result that could plausibly be reclassified as a partial resolution of this specific conjecture within the window.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement proving the conjecture (or a genuine special case restricting the stated hypotheses, e.g. for specific algebraic number fields or additional constraints on x1,x2,y1,y2) with a submission date after 26 January 2024, or an expert digestion (Tao's blog, a survey, Zentralblatt/MathSciNet review) crediting such a result.
